title: Programming Languages
description: Programming Languages studies how languages are designed, specified, implemented, and evaluated. Students compare syntax, semantics, type systems, lambda calculus, functional and logic programming, object-oriented and modular design, memory management, concurrency models, domain-specific languages, and compiler/runtime tradeoffs.

topics.title: Syntax, Grammars, and Abstract Syntax
topics.description: Students begin by learning how programming languages define valid programs and how concrete text becomes structured program representation.

children.title: Lexical structure
children.description: The point is to understand how raw characters are grouped into meaningful tokens.

children.title: Grammars and parsing
children.description: Students learn how formal grammars describe valid program structure.

children.title: Abstract syntax
children.description: Abstract syntax trees keep the essential structure while dropping surface notation.

topics.title: Operational, Denotational, and Axiomatic Semantics
topics.description: This module explains how programming-language meaning can be specified precisely rather than by vague examples or implementation accidents.

children.title: Operational semantics
children.description: Operational semantics explains program meaning by describing evaluation steps.

children.title: Denotational semantics
children.description: Denotational semantics maps programs to mathematical meanings.

children.title: Axiomatic semantics
children.description: Axiomatic semantics supports reasoning about program correctness.

topics.title: Interpreters and Language Implementation Foundations
topics.description: Students build executable models of language features so semantics becomes something they can run, test, and extend.

children.title: Interpreter structure
children.description: Interpreters make language ideas concrete by executing an AST according to semantic rules.

children.title: Environments and scope
children.description: Students learn how names are resolved and how scope affects program behavior.

children.title: Error handling
children.description: Language implementations must report and manage invalid programs clearly.

topics.title: Type Systems, Type Checking, and Type Inference
topics.description: This topic examines how languages use types to prevent errors, guide abstraction, and support compiler and tooling guarantees.

children.title: Type safety
children.description: Types help rule out classes of bad behavior before execution or at runtime boundaries.

children.title: Type checking
children.description: Students learn how rules assign and validate types for expressions and programs.

children.title: Type inference
children.description: Inference reduces annotation burden while preserving static guarantees.

topics.title: Lambda Calculus and Foundations of Computation
topics.description: Students study the small formal core behind functional programming, substitution, binding, evaluation, and many PL theory ideas.

children.title: Core syntax
children.description: Lambda calculus strips computation down to variables, functions, and application.

children.title: Substitution and binding
children.description: Correct handling of names is central to language semantics.

children.title: Evaluation strategies
children.description: Different evaluation choices produce different performance and termination behavior.

topics.title: Functional Programming and Algebraic Data
topics.description: This module develops functional language concepts such as immutable data, higher-order functions, recursion, pattern matching, and algebraic data types.

children.title: Functional abstraction
children.description: Functional languages emphasize computation by composing expressions and functions.

children.title: Recursive data and pattern matching
children.description: Algebraic data types make structured data and control flow explicit.

children.title: Purity and effects
children.description: Students learn how functional languages manage mutation, I/O, and state.

topics.title: Logic Programming and Declarative Paradigms
topics.description: Students learn how computation can be expressed as facts, rules, constraints, and search rather than step-by-step commands.

children.title: Logic-programming model
children.description: Logic programming treats computation as proving goals from facts and rules.

children.title: Search and unification
children.description: The language runtime searches for assignments that satisfy relations.

children.title: Constraints and applications
children.description: Declarative ideas appear in solvers and domain-specific systems.

topics.title: Object-Oriented and Modular Language Design
topics.description: This topic compares objects, classes, inheritance, interfaces, modules, traits, and encapsulation as tools for organizing programs.

children.title: Object model
children.description: Object-oriented languages organize behavior around encapsulated state and message dispatch.

children.title: Inheritance and composition
children.description: Students compare reuse mechanisms and their design costs.

children.title: Modules and abstraction
children.description: Modules manage boundaries in large programs.

topics.title: Memory Management, Runtime Systems, and Garbage Collection
topics.description: Students study what language runtimes do beneath the surface: allocation, lifetime, stack/heap organization, and automatic memory management.

children.title: Runtime layout
children.description: Language runtimes manage activation records, objects, and data representation.

children.title: Manual and automatic memory
children.description: Students compare explicit memory management with garbage-collected systems.

children.title: Garbage collection
children.description: Garbage collectors reclaim unreachable memory using different tradeoffs.

topics.title: Concurrency Models and Effectful Computation
topics.description: This module compares threads, actors, CSP, async/await, shared state, message passing, and effect management in language design.

children.title: Shared-state concurrency
children.description: Threads and locks are powerful but introduce races and coordination hazards.

children.title: Message passing
children.description: Message-passing models reduce shared-state coupling.

children.title: Async and effects
children.description: Modern languages expose asynchronous computation and effects through language constructs.

topics.title: Domain-Specific Languages and Metaprogramming
topics.description: Students learn when and how languages are specialized for domains, and how programs can generate, transform, or reason about other programs.

children.title: DSL motivation
children.description: Domain-specific languages trade generality for expressive power in a specific problem area.

children.title: Metaprogramming
children.description: Programs can generate or transform code to reduce repetition or create abstractions.

children.title: DSL implementation
children.description: Students learn practical choices for building a small language.

topics.title: Language Design Tradeoffs, Compilation, and Evaluation
topics.description: The course closes by connecting language features to compiler structure, optimization, usability, safety, performance, and design judgment.

children.title: Compiler structure
children.description: Compiler stages show how language design becomes executable machine behavior.

children.title: Optimization and performance
children.description: Language features affect what compilers can optimize.

children.title: Design evaluation
children.description: Students learn to assess a language feature from multiple angles.
